lead_responses.what_lead_said: Is it possible to generate more with a long-term let — I was comparing the prices, because a long-term let could be £700 plus bills?

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Do you have a minimum profitability threshold to take on a property — because you also have costs (cleaning company, maintenance) so it has to be worth the hassle for you too?

For your situation this works because you still need access and you're already paying for the property every month regardless, so any income is a cost-saving exercise as much as a profit-making one.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: How expensive are the maintenance services — I've heard some agencies charge a lot and some have their own in-house maintenance teams rather than using local companies?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Probably safe to expect about 5% of revenue toward upkeep and maintenance as a rule of thumb, though that's across the board — flats typically cost less to maintain than older houses.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: But services are generally quite expensive... okay anyway.

zac_language.numbers_framing: Led with the annual gross/net figures (£11,700 gross / £6,100 net), converted them to a monthly average (£508/month), and directly compared that to the lead's stated £500/month mortgage to make the cost-offset framing land immediately. Also broke out seasonal swing (January low ~£300-350, September peak ~£600-700) and floated an upside scenario (~£1,000/month once reviews grow past 27) to manage expectations while showing headroom, and openly acknowledged the automated comparables were skewed down by mismatched room-vs-flat listings.
zac_language.objection_handling_pattern: Acknowledges the lead's underlying point and confirms the numbers behind it (e.g. agrees long-letting would in theory earn more), then reframes back to the lead's own stated constraints and goals (mortgage type disallows long-letting, needs ongoing personal access, isn't trying to maximise profit) to show short-letting is still the right fit despite the lower theoretical ceiling.

personal-use booking calendar mechanics and flexibility
maintenance/repair cost structure and billing responsibility
whether Stayful has a minimum profitability threshold to accept the property
what_they_needed_most: reassurance that the arrangement isn't one-sided and genuinely benefits Stayful too
confirmation of full, uncapped personal-use flexibility for his unpredictable travel pattern

profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: For ABROAD/absentee-owner leads motivated by cost-offset rather than profit maximisation, lead with the 'cost saving against an unavoidable outgoing' framing earlier in the call rather than mid-call, and proactively volunteer the mutual-benefit / no-minimum-threshold reassurance before the lead has to ask for it — this profile's self-justifying language ('is this worth it for you too?') signals they need permission to feel like a low-effort, undemanding client.
